html:
A treaty signed on 22 April 1529 in which Castile, under the emperor Charles V, sold its claim to the Moluccas, the spice islands of eastern Indonesia, to Portugal under John III.

The Treaty of Tordesillas of 1494 had split the world between Spain and Portugal by a line in the Atlantic, but nobody knew where that line fell on the other side of the globe. When the survivors of Magellan's voyage reached the Moluccas in 1521, both crowns claimed the cloves and nutmeg there. At Zaragoza, Charles V, short of money, gave up the claim for 350,000 ducats, and a line was drawn east of the islands.

The Philippines lay on the Portuguese side of that line, but Spain settled them anyway from 1565, and Portugal did not press the point. Manila became the Asian end of the Manila galleons to Mexico.
sum: A treaty signed on 22 April 1529 in which Castile, under the emperor Charles V, sold its claim to the Moluccas, the spice islands of eastern Indonesia, to Portugal under John III.
